what: The Days Between Dates tool counts how much time there is between two dates. It shows the total number of days, the same time in weeks and days, in years, months and days, and how many of those days are weekdays (Monday to Friday) and weekend days.
It helps people planning projects, counting down to a holiday or exam, checking a notice period or deadline, working out how long a contract runs, or counting working days for a leave request.
All counting is done in your browser, so your dates are not sent anywhere.
uses: Find how many days are left until a holiday, wedding or exam.
See how many Monday to Friday days fall in a project or a leave period.
Count the days between a notice date and the last working day.
See a period as years, months and days to compare it with an agreement.
Count how many days have passed since you started a habit or a project.
tutorial: The “Start date” box is filled with today’s date when the page opens. Keep it, or click it and pick another date.
Click “End date” and pick the second date. The results appear as soon as both dates are filled in. If the end date is before the start date, the tool swaps them for you.
By default, the end date is not counted, so 1 May to 2 May is 1 day. Tick “Count the end date too” if both the first and the last day should be counted as full days.
“Days” is the total number of days. “Weeks” shows the same total as full weeks plus leftover days, for example 14w 3d.
This shows the period in calendar terms, counting full months first and then the remaining days.
“Weekdays (Mon–Fri)” counts Monday to Friday. “Weekend days” counts Saturdays and Sundays. Together they equal the total days.
features: An exact day count using real calendar dates, including leap years.
The total split into full weeks and leftover days.
A calendar-style breakdown of the period.
Separate counts of Monday to Friday and of Saturday and Sunday.
One checkbox adds the end date to every count.
If you enter the dates in the wrong order, they are swapped automatically.

example.title: Worked example: from 20 November 2026 to 1 March 2027
example.text: Set “Start date” to 20 November 2026, a Friday, and “End date” to 1 March 2027. “Days” shows 101 and “Weeks” shows 14w 3d, because 14 × 7 = 98 and 3 days are left. “Years, months, days” shows 0y 3m 9d: three months take you to 20 February, then 9 more days reach 1 March. “Weekdays (Mon–Fri)” shows 71 and “Weekend days” shows 30. Now tick “Count the end date too”: the days become 102, the weeks 14w 4d, and the weekdays 72, because 1 March 2027 is a Monday.

tips: Leave the end date unticked for deadlines and countdowns. Tick it when you count days you are present, such as days of a trip or leave.
Public holidays are counted as normal weekdays. Subtract your local holidays yourself.
February 2028 has 29 days, and the tool counts it correctly because it uses the real calendar.
To count days since a past event, put the event in “Start date” and leave today in the other box, or the other way round. The order does not matter.
The years, months and days result depends on month lengths, so the same number of days can show as different months in different parts of the year.
problems: One of the dates is empty. The end date is blank when the page opens, so pick it first.
The count is one less than I expected
The end date is not counted by default. Tick “Count the end date too”.
The weekday count includes a public holiday
The tool does not know holidays in your country. Subtract them by hand.
With the end date ticked, a full year shows as 0y 11m 31d

The extra day is added to the leftover days instead of rolling over into a new month. For example, 1 January to 31 December 2026 with the box ticked shows 365 days and 0y 11m 31d. The total days are correct.
